overall: The AG found the Auburn Housing Authority Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving three sets of July–September 2023 minutes months late and by never responding to a September 22 minutes request.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to timely approve minutes of its July 6, July 10, and September 7 meetings until December 14.
allegations.key_passage: As December 14 was more than 30 days and more than three meetings after each of the meeting dates at issue, the Board failed to timely approve minutes of those three meetings, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to respond at all to the complainant's September 22 request for meeting minutes.
allegations.key_passage: The Board has not disputed that it failed to respond to the Complainant’s September 22 request for minutes, and we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent and may result in civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law and may result in the imposition of civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
